gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Noto Sans Khmer reads clean and modern, its small letters standing proud, nearly capital-sized. Disorder shouts above it in raw, widely spaced glyphs of constant stroke, while Noto Sans Khmer keeps the text underneath open and settled.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Chaotic and raw, Disorder draws every stroke like cut ribbon, the same width from start to finish. And Noto Sans Khojki follows with clear, large eyes on each e, so the sans text stays easy to enter.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-khudawa: Noto Sans Khudawadi reads clean and approachable, with rounds left unsealed like an unlatched hook. Disorder is best at making noise, with strokes pulled like solder through a nozzle, and Noto Sans Khudawadi is best at lowering the volume again.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-kr: Raw, jagged and loud, Disorder leads. Beneath it, Noto Sans KR sets stubby ascenders and descenders beside a big x-height, giving the plain sans text a compact, generous footing against that constant pen line.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-lao: Disorder draws everything in one uninterrupted monoline stroke, with big lowercase and glyphs set well apart. But Noto Sans Lao answers in a modern, contemporary voice, its tall x-height keeping mouths open on c, e and a.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-lao-loo: Noto Sans Lao Looped is professional and modern, with bowls left unfinished on one side. Noto Sans Lao Looped also forms solid word blocks beside Disorder's constant-stroke chaos, and that gap between rough and ordered is what defines the pair.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Noto Sans Limbu has tall-bodied small letters and curves that gape, a contemporary, approachable plain sans. And Disorder, with its fixed-width stencil-brush line, does the raw shouting best, while Noto Sans Limbu carries the quieter work.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Rough, loose and a bit wild. Noto Sans Lisu follows with wide-open s curves and tiny gaps under its ascender tops, a professional sans-serif foil to Disorder's gentle monotone line and its chaotic spacing.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Disorder's round bowls never swell or taper anywhere. It does raw, chaotic display best, with large lowercase and loose spacing, while the plain sans Noto Sans Lydian does approachable text best, its capitals barely taller than lowercase.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-mahajan: Noto Sans Mahajani is modern and professional, its lowercase standing tall against the capitals. Noto Sans Mahajani brings a wide funnel-like throat in the e, and next to Disorder's constant raw stroke that openness is the pair's sharpest quality.
